title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
summary: A simulation-derived biological-torque estimator transferred to a physical knee exoskeleton and reduced measured knee moment and vastus medialis activation during squatting in seven able-bodied participants. This is not evidence of clinical benefit. A muscle-driven imitation policy trained on open biomechanics data supplies a learned onboard-sensor torque estimator. Physical exoskeleton measurements in seven participants with within-task no-assistance comparison; limited to reported squatting protocol.
